Next, eye color. I've heard that while genetics play a big role, things like sun exposure and maybe even certain medications can change eye color temporarily. So maybe eye color is influenced by the environment too, but not as much as body weight.

Blood type, from what I remember, is mostly determined by genetics. There are specific alleles that determine blood types, and while things like diet can affect blood sugar levels, blood type itself is more about the presence of certain proteins on red blood cells, which is genetic. So I don't think blood type is much influenced by the environment.

Color blindness is a genetic condition as well. It's something you're born with, based on the genes you inherit. While environmental factors like exposure to certain chemicals might affect vision, color blindness itself is a genetic trait. So I don't think the environment has much effect on color blindness.

Comparing all these, body weight seems to be the most influenced by environmental factors. Eye color has some influence too, but not as much as body weight. So the most influenced trait is probably body weight.
